nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$. Then the complete $r$-graph on $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ (the family of all its $r$-element subsets) is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system.
nodes.title: The complete $r$-graph is a Turán system

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $r$, every member of the complete $r$-graph on $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ has exactly $r$ elements.
nodes.title: The complete $r$-graph is $r$-uniform

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $r$, the complete $r$-graph on $n$ vertices is the family of all $r$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: The complete $r$-graph

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then every $s$-element subset $T$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ contains some member $e$ of $H$.
nodes.title: Turán systems cover every $s$-set

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$ with $0 < r < s \le n$, there is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system.
nodes.title: Turán systems exist

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers. A family $H$ of subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system when $0 < r < s \le n$, $H$ is $r$-uniform (every member of $H$ has exactly $r$ elements), and every $s$-element subset of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ contains some member of $H$.
nodes.title: Turán system

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then $s \le n$.
nodes.title: A Turán system has $s \le n$

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$, $b$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$. If $b \le k$ for every $k$ in the set of realized sizes for $(n, s, r)$ (the sizes of Turán $(n, s, r)$-systems), then $b$ is at most the Turán number $T(n, s, r)$.
nodes.title: Lower bounds on the Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then $r < s$.
nodes.title: A Turán system has $r < s$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, $k$, the number $k$ lies in the set of realized sizes for $(n, s, r)$ if and only if some Turán $(n, s, r)$-system $H$ has exactly $k$ members.
nodes.title: Membership in the realized sizes

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, whose definition includes $0 < r < s \le n$. Then $0 < r$.
nodes.title: Turán systems have positive uniformity

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$ with $0 < r < s \le n$, the set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$ is nonempty: some natural number $k$ is the number of members of a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$.
nodes.title: Some size of a Turán system is realized

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, the set of realized sizes is the set of natural numbers $k$ such that some Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has exactly $k$ members.
nodes.title: Realized sizes of Turán systems

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$ and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. Then some Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$ has exactly $T(n, s, r)$ members.
nodes.title: The Turán number is attained

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. If $H$ is a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, then $T(n, s, r) \le |H|$.
nodes.title: Turán systems are at least as large as the Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$ and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. Then $T(n, s, r)$ belongs to the set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$.
nodes.title: The Turán number is a realized size

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, the Turán number $T(n, s, r)$ is the least element of the set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$, that is, the least number of members of a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, and $T(n, s, r) = 0$ if no such system exists.
nodes.title: Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers. If $H$ is a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, then $H$ is $r$-uniform: every member of $H$ has exactly $r$ elements.
nodes.title: Turán systems are uniform

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
